text:
FPMC combines user–item preferences with a directed transition score \(m_j^Tn_i\); separate source/target embeddings allow \(j\to i\neq i\to j\). FOSSIL combines a history aggregate with weighted recent-item embeddings, scored against separate target embeddings: \(b_i+[h_u+\sum_k(\eta_k+\eta_k^u)P_{s_{t-k}}]^TQ_i\). Its higher-order transitions remain asymmetric despite sharing embeddings across long/short-term terms. [FOSSIL paper, including FPMC formulation](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.09152). SASRec scores \(h_t^TE_i\), where causal attention, positions and nonlinear transformations make \(h_t\) history-dependent; tied item embeddings do not force symmetric next-item predictions. Thus directed transitions alone are established prior art. [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781).

Proposed controls, derived algebraically: write \(M=A^TB=S+K\), with \(S=(M+M^T)/2\), \(K=(M-M^T)/2\). Compare baseline, full \(M\), symmetric-only \(S\), and skew-only \(K\), retraining each. The symmetric control \((A^TB+B^TA)/2\) uses exactly the same \(2kd\) trainable parameters for \(A,B\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\), permits negative eigenvalues, and removes the skew component. Its rank can reach \(2k\), versus \(k\) for full \(M\), so report rank alongside parameter count. An additional parameter-matched signed-Gram control is \(C^TJC\), with \(C\in\mathbb R^{2k\times d}\), fixed \(J=\mathrm{diag}(I_k,-I_k)\). Unlike these, \(A^TA\) is positive semidefinite and has only \(kd\) parameters, confounding symmetry, spectral constraints and capacity.

Match initialization scale, regularization, optimization and validation tuning budgets; supplement retraining with post-training removal of \(K\). These comparisons support an incremental asymmetry claim, not identification of all directionality: even symmetric \(S\) can yield directed predictions when \(r_t\) is a transformed history representation. Novelty would concern the particular SASRec residual and demonstrated benefit beyond matched bilinear capacity.
